# Independent audit: sharp midpoint capacity does not select a safe centroid


candidate b5b24ea04cec9d49
in full. The standard-library verifier
supporting computation verify_all_dimensional_sharp_midpoint_density_centroid_counterexample.py
reran successfully on 100 exact dimensional instances. The proof
itself treats every integer d>=1. No correction is required.

## Actual source and density normalization

The lifted hull of epsilon T,T,T at bases -1,0,1 has exactly these
three positive integer fibers. The only possible middle enlargement
from the two endpoints is rT, and rT is contained in T. The hull is
full dimensional. Every fiber mass is strictly below half of
(2+epsilon^d)V.

The endpoint dilation is an actual positive affine coupling of their
uniform probabilities. Multiplying its midpoint law by |A| gives
the density (a/r^d)1_(rT), whose mass is aV. The sharp capacity is
exactly r^d V. Any other absolutely continuous midpoint law subject
to that same density bound and endpoint coupling has support in rT;
the upper bound integrates to its whole prescribed mass, so equality
forces that same density almost everywhere.

Multiplication by L=(1+a)/a and addition of 1_T produce mass
(2+a)V. Its continuous centroid is h g with
h=(31+11a)/(40+20a). Since 0<h<1, the selected base-zero point is
an actual point of the middle fiber.

## Original oblique cap and strict comparison

For H={sum x_i+z<=q}, q=d h/(d+1), the endpoint thresholds are
q+1 and q-1. They are respectively strictly above epsilon and
strictly below zero. Thus the first endpoint contributes aV,
the other contributes zero, and the middle contributes q^d V.
The plane passes through the proposed point and its continuous
normal is nonzero. Closed boundary conventions add no hidden
d-dimensional mass.

The estimate h<=31/40 is a direct cross multiplication. Since
d/(d+1)>=1/2,
a/Gamma <=(1/5)^d. Hence the exact cap mass divided by Gamma V
is at most (31/40)^d+(1/5)^d <=39/40, whereas the target divided
by Gamma V is 1+a/2>1. This proves a strict failure in every
dimension, including d=1, without a numerical or asymptotic premise.

The auxiliary midpoint-cost comparison also has the right direction:
the midpoint indicator is at most the sum of the two coupled endpoint
indicators. The second endpoint marginal has density a<=1 relative
to its actual volume law. Consequently the midpoint measure cost
is at most the actual endpoint-inclusive cost; no replacement of
the actual source by a larger surrogate is made.

## Separate safe candidate

The cited measurable-subset theorem applies directly to
E=epsilon T contained in K=T and retains one common normal with
the paired opposite thresholds. Its middle centroid lower bound
is (Gamma+lambda_d a)V, where lambda_1=1 and lambda_d>1/2
for d>=2. Since Gamma<=1/2, this strictly exceeds
Gamma(2+a)V/2. Pure vertical caps contain the whole middle
fiber and also satisfy the target.

This safety proof is independent of the failed density-centroid
rule and does not invoke unrestricted OC. The counterexample
therefore refutes the exact named selection rule while preserving
both sharp midpoint capacity and the original body's OC safety.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
